entry.title: Stop Reading, Start Knowing: The Philosophy of Mippedia Concise
entry.summary: Time is the ultimate currency. At Mippedia Concise, we have one mission: Don’t make the user read more than they need to. Mippedia Concise is our answer to "Information Overload." We take complex encyclopedic topics and strip away the filler. What’s left is a high-density, fact-checked summary that gives you the "What, Who, and When" in seconds. It’s the "TL;DR" for the academic and historical world. Efficient, accurate, and straight to the point.

entry.title: Beyond the Standard Wiki: How Mippedia Reinvents Information Accessibility
entry.summary: In a world drowning in data, finding professional-grade, independent information is harder than it looks. That’s why we built Mippedia Indonesia and its English counterpart. Most people rely on giant platforms, but we believe in a decentralized approach to knowledge. Our flagship branches are dedicated to high-standard, encyclopedic articles that cover history, technology, and culture with professional administrative rigor. We’ve customized our MediaWiki environment to ensure that every article meets a specific standard of quality and clarity. By maintaining independence, we ensure that our community’s voice and data remain sovereign.

entry.title: Building a Modern Open Knowledge Ecosystem: Introducing Mippedia
entry.summary:
Hello World! 🚀 We are excited to join the DEV community and share our journey in building Mippedia, an independent open-knowledge ecosystem designed for the modern era. What is Mippedia? Mippedia isn't just another wiki. It’s a multi-branch project built on the MediaWiki engine, specifically designed to bridge the gap between long-form encyclopedic content and structured, easy-to-digest data. The Ecosystem Breakdown: Mippedia Indonesia: Our flagship encyclopedic branch focusing on professional-standard articles in Indonesian.
Mippedia Data: This is where we geek out. It’s a structured database dedicated to entities like history, technology, and musicians. We focus on tables and raw data over long paragraphs.
Mippedia Concise: For users who value time. We provide TL;DR versions of complex topics without losing factual accuracy.
Mippedia English: Our bridge to the global audience, ensuring knowledge transcends language barriers.
Behind the Project Mippedia is maintained by the Mippedia Community, a group of enthusiasts dedicated to digital archiving and open-knowledge management. The project was founded by Rumi Haitami, an entrepreneur and musician who saw the need for a more structured way to store and access digital information. Why DEV? We’re here to share our technical challenges—from configuring MediaWiki administrative protocols to managing multi-domain database synchronization. Stay tuned as we dive deeper into our tech stack and documentation! Check us out at: mippedia.org

entry.title: Zero Token Architecture: Why Your AI Agent Should Never See Your Real API Key
entry.summary: Hot take: every AI agent security guide I've read is solving the wrong problem. We spend hours sandboxing the runtime. We lock down the filesystem. We audit every package. We wrap the agent in Docker, then wrap Docker in a VM, then wrap the VM in policy. And then we hand the agent a plaintext API key and call it secure. Stop protecting the token. Just don't hand it over. Prompt injection + arbitrary package execution means any token your AI agent can see is a token it can leak. Instead of protecting the token after the agent has it, pass the agent a fake token whose value equals its own name. Intercept the agent's outbound API call at the boundary and swap in the real token there. If the fake leaks, the attacker gets a useless string. The real token never leaves your trusted process. entry.summary: When we talk about technical debt, we usually talk about lists. A linter report with 450 warnings. A backlog with 32 "refactoring" tickets. A SonarQube dashboard showing 15% duplication. But for AI-generated code, lists are deceiving.
